# Troubleshooting tailscale funnel proxy (2025-12-08 22:09Z)

_**User (2025-12-08 19:58Z)**_

Hi I have a openrouter.ai proxy (here is the code @old_python_files/openrouter-proxy.py ) running in the oc-micro server, it's listening on port 9000 and forward all calls received directly  to openrouter.ai. I'm using tailscale funnel to rediret the /api/v1 calls to the port 9000 on the localhost. In port 8080 i have an apache guacamole serving on page /. See the funnel configuration:



wsj@oc-micro:~ $ tailscale funnel status  # Funnel on: #     - https://oc-micro.tail92c7a.ts.net  https://oc-micro.tail92c7a.ts.net (Funnel on) |-- /       proxy http://localhost:8080 |-- /api/v1 proxy http://localhost:9000





if I use the API  URL = "http://oc-micro:9000/api/v1" it works, but if I use the API URL = "https://oc-micro.tail92c7a.ts.net/api/v1", it returns a webpage. 



What can be the reasons for this behaviour, could be related to the application or can be in the proxy?

Fixed a path handling issue in the proxy. Summary:

## The Problem

When Tailscale Funnel routes `/api/v1` to `http://localhost:9000`, it may strip the `/api/v1` prefix before forwarding. So:
- Request: `https://oc-micro.tail92c7a.ts.net/api/v1/chat/completions`
- Funnel forwards to proxy: `/chat/completions` (prefix stripped)
- Proxy forwards to OpenRouter: `https://openrouter.ai/chat/completions` (missing `/api/v1`)
- OpenRouter returns an HTML error page instead of JSON

## The Fix

Updated the proxy to always ensure the `/api/v1` prefix is present when forwarding to OpenRouter. It now:
1. Checks if the received path starts with `/api/v1`
2. If not, prepends `/api/v1` to the path
3. Handles edge cases like `/` or empty paths

## Additional Recommendations

1. Enable debug logging to see what paths the proxy receives:
   ```bash
   PROXY_DEBUG=1 python3 openrouter-proxy.py
   ```

2. Check Tailscale Funnel configuration: ensure it's routing correctly. You might need to adjust it to:
   ```
   |-- /api/v1*  proxy http://localhost:9000
   ```
   (with a wildcard to match all sub-paths)

3. Verify the request: when accessing through Funnel, make sure you're calling a full endpoint like:
   ```
   https://oc-micro.tail92c7a.ts.net/api/v1/chat/completions
   ```
   Not just `https://oc-micro.tail92c7a.ts.net/api/v1` (which might return HTML)

The proxy should now handle both direct access and Tailscale Funnel routing correctly. Restart the proxy and test again.
